getReady.camera.title: What the camera is for
getReady.camera.checks: During the exam the camera checks only that you are there, on your own, and looking at the screen. It works on this device: no video or picture of you is recorded or sent.
getReady.camera.never: The camera never grades you and never decides anything. Anything it notices is a low-confidence note for a person to read, never an automatic result.
getReady.eyes.title: About eye contact
getReady.eyes.look: While the examiner asks and while you answer, look at her as you would on a video call.
getReady.eyes.look.male: While the examiner asks and while you answer, look at him as you would on a video call.
getReady.eyes.thinkingOk: Looking away to think is completely normal.
getReady.eyes.thinkingWhy: Most people do it, and it often helps. You never need to stare at the screen, and nothing happens when you glance away.
getReady.eyes.reminder: Only a long look away from the screen while you are answering gets a reminder, and it is a gentle one: never a warning sound or a flashing screen.
getReady.eyes.neverGrade: Reminders never change your grade, and nothing ends your exam automatically.
getReady.eyes.off: This exam doesn't use the eye-contact check.

getReady.how.title: How Socratic questioning works
getReady.how.intro: This isn't a multiple-choice test. The examiner asks one question at a time and builds the next question from your own answer: it may ask you to clarify a word you used, give an example, test your idea against a tricky case, or point out when two of your answers seem to disagree.
getReady.science.summary: Why it works this way (the science behind it)
getReady.science.p1: This is the method Socrates used, called the elenchus: he questioned people who were sure they knew something and found that one of them "thinks he knows something when he does not" (Plato, Apology 21d). The questions only ever use what you yourself said, and they check whether your answers fit together.
getReady.science.whyTitle: Why follow-up questions show real understanding.
getReady.science.why: A single right answer can be remembered or guessed. Explaining why it is true, handling a case that doesn't fit and using the idea in a new situation is much harder without understanding it. Psychologists use the same approach to find out how people think: vary the questions, try a counter-suggestion, and never put the answer in the person's mouth (Piaget, 1929). Being asked to explain also tends to help people learn (Bisra et al., 2018), so the exam can teach you something too.
getReady.science.limitsTitle: Its limits, and what Gadfly does about them.
getReady.science.limit1: If two of your answers disagree, that shows something isn't settled yet, not which answer is wrong (Vlastos, 1983; Benson, 1995). You can fix either one; your course material and the grading rubric decide what is right.
getReady.science.limit2: Explaining out loud slows everyone down (Fox, Ericsson & Best, 2011). Pauses, "um"s, an accent and how fast you speak are not graded.
getReady.science.limit3: Speech recognition can mishear some accents and stuttered speech (Koenecke et al., 2020; Mujtaba et al., 2024). If the next question shows the examiner misheard you, say so and put it again in your own words.
getReady.science.limit4: One exam can't measure everything, and AI graders make mistakes (van der Vleuten et al., 2010; Zheng et al., 2023). Several AI models score each topic separately, a human examiner grades too, and a person approves your result before you see it.
getReady.science.limit5: A webcam can't tell reading from thinking (Papoutsaki et al., 2016), and voice measures can't detect stress or lying (Harnsberger et al., 2009). Camera notes and the comparison of your voice with your first answers are shown to a reviewer only as low-confidence notes, never as a verdict and never as part of your grade. The voice comparison can lead the examiner to ask an extra follow-up question.
getReady.science.refs: Full references and how each was checked: "The science behind Gadfly" in Gadfly's documentation (docs/SCIENCE.md).
getReady.rules.typed: The examiner talks to you and asks each question out loud. Your instructor has given you an accommodation: you type your answers instead of speaking them, and your microphone isn't used. Your camera must stay on for the whole exam, and the eye-contact check applies as for everyone (unless you also have the eye-contact accommodation). If the camera stops working, the exam pauses until you bring it back.
getReady.rules.typedOwnWords: Type in your own words. Pasting text into the answer box is noted for your instructor to review.
getReady.rules.spoken: The exam is spoken. The examiner talks to you and you answer out loud. Typing your answers is only possible as an accommodation your instructor grants (for a documented speech, hearing or anxiety need); ask them if you need it. Your microphone and camera must stay on for the whole exam. If either stops working, the exam pauses until you bring it back.
getReady.rules.clock: Your time starts when the examiner asks the first question, not when you press Begin exam.
getReady.rules.ownWords: Answer in your own words. Short, honest answers are better than long copied ones.
getReady.rules.dontKnow: If you genuinely don't know, say so or press I don't know. Admitting it is a real answer, not a failure, and the examiner moves on.
getReady.rules.reload: The clock is kept on the server; if you reload the page, you return to the same question.
getReady.rules.scores: You won't see scores during the exam. Your result is published once it has been graded and approved.
getReady.try.title: Try one (practice, not recorded)
getReady.try.question: Practice: in your own words, what is a habit?
getReady.try.typedHint: Type an answer in a sentence or two, then press the button. Nothing is recorded.
getReady.try.spokenHint: Answer out loud in a sentence or two, then press the button. Nothing is recorded.
getReady.try.waitMic: The button turns on once the system check above has heard your microphone.
getReady.try.followUp: Can you think of something that fits your description, but that you wouldn't call a habit?
getReady.try.followUpWhy: That's a counterexample move: the examiner tests your definition against a case built from your own words. In the real exam the follow-ups are written live from what you say.
getReady.try.dontKnowFollowUp: That's fine. Let's come at it from another side: can you name one thing you do almost every day without thinking about it?
getReady.try.dontKnowWhy: "I don't know" is an honest answer. The examiner records it and either tries an easier angle or moves on to the next topic.

getReady.language.title: Your languages
getReady.language.why: We ask so the examiner can be fair to students taking the exam in a language that isn't their first. Your answers are never used to grade you, and nothing about where you come from is ever worked out from them.
getReady.language.primary: Which language do you speak best?
getReady.language.editable: Your answers are saved when you begin and filled in for you next time; you can change them here before any exam.
getReady.language.exam: Which language do you want to take this exam in?
getReady.language.lock: This page, the rules and the examiner switch to it straight away. You can change it until you press Begin exam; then it stays for this attempt.
getReady.calibration.summary: Help the examiner hear you (about a minute)
getReady.calibration.summaryOptional: Help the examiner hear you (optional; you can skip this)
getReady.calibration.why: Read one short sentence aloud three times. It helps the speech recognizer get used to how you speak, so it waits for you at your own pace and mishears you less. Only a few numbers are kept (how fast you read, how long your pauses are, how sure the recognizer was): never a recording and never your words. It is never used to grade you. You can skip it, or do it again any time.
getReady.calibration.readThis: Read this aloud at your normal pace:
getReady.calibration.reading: Read it now ({0} of {1}). Take your time; pause when you're done.
getReady.calibration.done: Thank you, that's all. The examiner will use it to hear you better.
getReady.calibration.notHeard: We couldn't hear the sentence that time. Check the microphone above and try again, or skip this.
getReady.calibration.couldntStart: This couldn't start right now. That's fine: the exam works without it.
getReady.calibration.skipped: Stopped. Nothing from that round was kept.
getReady.calibration.waitMic: This turns on once the microphone check above has heard you.

getReady.js.mic.listening: Listening for a few seconds to check your microphone…
getReady.js.mic.someNoise: Background noise: a little noticeable. A quieter room will help the recognizer hear you clearly.
getReady.js.mic.noisy: Background noise: noisy where you are. Close windows, turn off fans or move somewhere quieter if you can.
getReady.js.mic.clipping: Your microphone is picking up very loud peaks (clipping). Move it a little further away or turn its input volume down.
getReady.js.mic.noEchoCancel: Echo cancellation isn't on for this microphone. If you hear the examiner echo back through your own audio, use headphones.
getReady.js.mic.echo: If the examiner's voice echoes back through your microphone, headphones usually fix it.
getReady.js.gaze.title: Eye tracking
getReady.js.gaze.intro: During the exam your camera checks, on this device only, that you are looking at the examiner while you answer. This looks at your setup so that check works well for you. It never stops you starting.
getReady.js.gaze.loading: Starting the camera check… The first time can take a few seconds.
getReady.js.gaze.measuring: Look at your camera picture above for a few seconds.
getReady.js.gaze.unavailable: The eye-tracking check couldn't run on this device. That's fine: the exam carries on and uses a simpler check.
getReady.js.gaze.setupHint: Recommended: follow a dot with your eyes so the camera learns your screen. It makes the check fairer, with fewer false "looking away" moments.
getReady.js.gaze.caption: Follow the dot with your eyes and keep your head still. Esc or Skip stops.
getReady.js.gaze.retry: Not quite precise enough. Once more: sit still and look right at the centre of each dot.
getReady.js.gaze.skipped: Setup skipped. The exam will use a simpler check of where your head and eyes point; you can set it up here or in the exam.
getReady.js.gaze.camera: The camera stopped during the setup. Check that it is still connected, then try again.
getReady.js.gaze.good: Set up: about {deg}° accuracy. The exam room checks it once more when you start.
getReady.js.gaze.poor: Not precise enough this time (about {deg}°), so the exam will use a simpler check of where your head and eyes point. That's fine. More light on your face, or sitting still, may help if you try again.
getReady.js.gaze.failed: The camera couldn't follow your eyes well enough to set this up. The exam will use a simpler check of where your head and eyes point. That's fine. More light on your face may help if you try again.
getReady.js.gaze.face.result.not-clearly: not clearly in view most of the time
getReady.js.gaze.face.fix.sit-facing-the: Sit facing the camera with your whole face in the picture.
getReady.js.gaze.face.result.more-than-o: more than one face in view
getReady.js.gaze.face.fix.during-the-exa: During the exam only you should be in the camera picture.
getReady.js.gaze.lighting.fix.turn-on-a-: Turn on a lamp in front of you (behind your screen) so it lights your face.
getReady.js.gaze.lighting.fix.turn-so-th: Turn so the light falls on your face, or close the blind behind you: the camera can't see your eyes against a bright background.
getReady.js.gaze.angle.fix.put-the-camer: Put the camera at about eye level, centred at the top of your screen, and face the screen.
getReady.js.gaze.distance.fix.move-a-lit: Move a little closer, to about an arm's length.
getReady.js.gaze.distance.fix.sit-back-a: Sit back a little, so your whole face fits in the picture.
getReady.js.gaze.distance.fix.centre-you: Centre your face in the camera picture.
getReady.js.gaze.eyes.fix.if-you-wear-gl: If you wear glasses, reflections on the lenses are the usual cause: tilt the screen or the lamp until you see no bright spots on them. More light on your face also helps.

practice.intro.male: A short, friendly run-through with the examiner who will give your exams. He explains each part of a real exam and has you try it:

practice.nothingKeptMore: It isn't graded, reported or counted as an attempt, and none of your exams are affected. It takes about five minutes, and you can leave, skip a step or start again at any time.
practice.needs: You need a working microphone and camera, and your sound on (a headset works best). Your browser will ask to use the microphone and camera: allow both. As in an exam, your camera picture stays on your device; no video or sound is recorded.

notice.hold.title: Your exam is paused
notice.hold.text: Your instructor paused your exam. Your time is stopped and nothing you say counts until they resume it. Please stay here.
result.notPublished: This result hasn't been published to you.
result.transcript: Your transcript, with its verification code:
result.integrity.title: Integrity notes on this attempt
result.integrity.none: Nothing was noted about how this exam was taken.
result.integrity.intro: During the exam, checks on your device and the answers noted a few moments for a person to look at. You see here exactly what your instructor sees, with the same explanation. These notes are context, never a finding of cheating, and none of them is part of your grade: the grade comes from your answers. If something here is wrong or has an explanation, you can say so in an appeal below.
result.appeal.title: Appeal
result.appeal.open: Your appeal of {0} is being reviewed. Your published result stays visible meanwhile.
result.appeal.how: If you believe the grade is wrong, explain why. A teacher reviews it and either confirms the grade or amends it; you'll see the outcome here.
result.appeal.response: Your response to the integrity notes (optional)
result.appeal.responseHint: Say what happened at those moments, if you want to. It goes to the teacher with your appeal. You can send a response on its own, without a reason above.
result.appeal.tooLong: Your reason and response together are {0:N0} characters; please keep them to 4,000.
notifications.optOut: Don't email me reminders before an exam is due
notifications.explain: This only affects the reminder email sent a couple of days before an exam closes. You'll still be emailed when an exam is assigned to you and when your result is released — those don't stop, since they matter operationally. Your organization can also turn off Gadfly's emails entirely; if they have, this choice won't change anything either way.
